thread:
mira: Quick follow-up from RFC review: we still need a clear operational model for canary/A-B rollouts + automatic fallback across controller/router/runtime. Wanted to flush out one concrete pattern for the RFC appendix. Thoughts?

dan: TLDR proposal: keep controller as policy owner, router as coordinator/lease-checker and audit relay, runtime as last-millisecond fast-path. But define a compact handshake so local fallbacks are auditable and reproducible.

hao: Agree. Suggest we encode three signals in the handshake: policy_seed, policy_mode (enforce|simulate|drain), and controller_confidence (0-100). Router/runtime compute a final decision score = f(controller_confidence, local_health) and compare to policy threshold.

sylvie: FWIW ops wants determinism during partitions. If controller unreachable, routers must fall back to deterministic split using policy_seed + request_id hashing. No probabilistic decisions without seed. Example: `variant = hash(seed||req_id)%100 < pct`.

mira: Good. We also discussed layered fallback earlier — can we formalize it? I propose three layers: 1) runtime local short-circuit (fast, strict), 2) router hedging+sampling (confirm with controller), 3) controller-wide diversion/rollback. Each layer emits the same minimal audit event to rollout.signals.

dan: Addendum: local short-circuit should only trigger on severe local signals (OOM spike, threadpool saturation, immediate exceptions) or when deterministic rule says fallback. For transient metric blips use router-level fractional diversion first.

hao: Implementation sketch for the score combine: `final = clamp( floor(controller_confidence * w_c + local_health_score * w_l) , 0, 100 )` with defaults w_c=0.7, w_l=0.3. local_health_score ranges 0..100 (100 = healthy). If final < policy_min_confidence -> fallback.

sylvie: Ops asks we make weights configurable per-policy and include a simulate flag. Also require a min_stable_window before re-enabling a variant to avoid oscillation. E.g., min_stable_window=2m, cool_down=5m.

mira: Audit schema (mini): single-line event containing fields: ts, node_id, policy_id, policy_v, action_code, final_score, reason_codes (comma list), sample_request_id(optional). Keep payload < 512 bytes. Example: `2026-03-23T10:12:00Z node-17 p42 v3 DECISION_FALLBACK 37 OOM,ERR_RATE sample=abc123`

dan: Router API notes: PATCH /v1/rollouts/:id -> push policy (policy_id, seed, pct, min_confidence, ttl, weights, mode). Router caches until ttl. Router exposes GET /v1/rollouts/:id/debug returning last N sampled local decisions (ops-only).

hao: Runtime API notes: local endpoint `/local/fallback?req_hash=...` returns a compact decision: code (0=follow,1=fallback,2=simulate), policy_v, final_score, reason. Use numeric codes to ease telemetry aggregation.

sylvie: Error codes mapping: 200 + code body for decision, 409 for policy mismatch (when policy id/version doesn't match runtime cached), 503 for overloaded/no-capacity. Router should surface these to caller.

mira: Hedging: default OFF. If enabled in policy, router will attempt a single parallel hedge request to the fallback variant with a strict extra latency budget (<=40ms). If the hedge completes faster, use the response and emit hedged_event. Count hedging cost separate from base latency.

dan: Sampling strategy to keep costs low: sample 0.5% of normal traffic to full raw events, and emit 1-min aggregates for all policies/regions. Increase sampling to 5-10% only during suspect windows (controller alerts). Backoff sampling if controller ack latency >200ms.

hao: Determinism details: when seed present routers use `hash(seed||request_id)` for split decisions. For session-affinity, seed changes per rollout_epoch so stickiness lasts only for rollout. Documented pseudo included in RFC appendix.

sylvie: Security: no raw prompts in events. Use request_hash and optionally sampled request_id. Audit logs retention controlled by org policy. GDPR note: scrub PII in sample payloads.

mira: Ops runbook snippets: if `local-fallback-mode` events spike across routers -> check controller connectivity and policy TTLs. If controller healthy but many fallbacks: raise alert on `rollout.err_rate_5m` and consider rollback via controller API. Provide manual endpoints: POST /v1/rollouts/:id/force-off and POST /v1/rollouts/:id/force-on (ops-only).

dan: Edge cases: policy update during partition. Use versioned policy_v and ensure routers accept older policy_v until new policy propagated + ttl. If mismatch, return 409 and log. Add a graceful drain path where new policy includes `drain=true` to allow phased switch.

hao: Performance note: runtime hedging must be bounded to avoid CPU/GPU thrash. Limit hedges per-second per-node (e.g., 10 RPS hedges max). If exceeded, return decision follow-control to avoid cascade.

sylvie: Observability: dashboards should show: controller_confidence, aggregated final_score, decision_code distribution, hedging_ratio, sampled_fallback_events. Alert when final_score divergence between controller and aggregated runtimes > 20 for 5m.

mira: Action items: (1) hao: produce compact proto + sample JSON, (2) dan: router API + debug endpoint spec + lease semantics, (3) sylvie: audit event exact line spec + retention and alert thresholds. I'll merge into RFC appendix and circulate to arch.

deploy-bot: rollout-policy "canary-small-2026-03-23" v1 applied to region us-west-2 at 2026-03-23T10:14:05Z

mira: Thanks everyone. We'll aim to pilot simulate-mode on a low-risk model next week and collect sampled events. /cc @hao @dan @sylvie
